description: Polyphonic macro oscillator with twenty-four synthesis models, from filtered waveforms and six-operator FM through speech, granular clouds and physical models to analogue drums

params.text: Steps through the twenty-four models in three banks of eight — new, pitched, and noise and percussive — and the display spells the eight-letter code of the one in use
Sets the pitch; how far it reaches follows the frequency mode, which by default is the eight octaves from C0 to C8
Sets the harmonic content of the model in use, which in most of them is the spread of the spectrum
Sets the first timbre parameter of the model in use, which in most of them is the brightness of the tone
Sets the second timbre parameter of the model in use, which in most of them gives a sideways variation of the tone
Attenuverts the TIMBRE input; with nothing patched to TIMBRE but a cable at TRIG, any setting other than zero hands that modulation to the internal decaying envelope instead
Attenuverts the FM input; with nothing patched to FM but a cable at TRIG, any setting other than zero hands that modulation to the internal decaying envelope instead
Attenuverts the MORPH input; with nothing patched to MORPH but a cable at TRIG, any setting other than zero hands that modulation to the internal decaying envelope instead
Sets the response of the internal low-pass gate, from a filter that closes down with the level at the counter-clockwise end to a plain amplifier at the clockwise end
Sets the ringing time of the internal low-pass gate, and with it the decay of the internal envelope
Sets the root note that the FREQUENCY knob's octave steps are counted from; it is read only while the frequency mode is set to octaves
Sets what the FREQUENCY knob covers: an LFO range, the eight octaves from C0 to C8, whole octaves above a root note, or seven semitones either side of one fixed C
Attenuverts the low-pass gate response input
Attenuverts the low-pass gate decay input

inputs.text: Shifts the model up or down from the one the knob picks, with each polyphonic channel taking its own offset; with a cable at TRIG the offset is read at each trigger and held until the next one
Adds to the TIMBRE knob through its attenuverter, 8V covering the whole knob range
Shifts the pitch through the FM attenuverter, six semitones per volt at full attenuverter
Adds to the MORPH knob through its attenuverter, 8V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the HARMONICS knob through its attenuverter, 5V covering the whole knob range
A rising edge past 0.9V starts the internal envelope, excites the percussive and physical models, holds the model offset, and strikes the low-pass gate when LEVEL is unpatched
Opens the internal low-pass gate, 8V giving full level, and accents the percussive and physical models; with nothing patched the trigger strikes the gate instead
Sets the pitch, one volt per octave, reaching three octaves below the root note and seven above it
Adds to the LPG. RSP. knob through its attenuverter, 5V covering the whole knob range; this jack reads one channel only, and that one voltage is applied to every polyphonic channel
Adds to the LPG. DCY. knob through its attenuverter, 5V covering the whole knob range; this jack reads one channel only, and that one voltage is applied to every polyphonic channel

outputs.text: A second signal from the same model, ±5V, which is a variant of the main output or a by-product of it and differs from model to model

notes: the module is polyphonic: the channel count comes from whichever of TRIG and V/OCT carries more channels, and each channel runs its own voice.
the two low-pass gate jacks are monophonic, which is what their silver rings mean: only the first channel of a cable is read, and that voltage is applied to every channel the module is running.
with nothing patched to TRIG the model plays continuously and the low-pass gate stays open; patching TRIG turns the module into a struck voice with its own envelope.
five of the models read custom data that can be replaced from the Custom data menu: the three six-operator FM models, the wave terrain model and the wavetable model.
menu: Synthesis model: New, Pitched, Noise/percussive — three submenus listing the twenty-four models in the order the MODEL knob steps through them
Frequency mode: LFO mode, C0 +/- 7 semitones, through C7 +/- 7 semitones, Octaves, C0 to C8 — sets what the FREQUENCY knob covers, the same setting the F. MODE knob carries
Options — the submenu holding the display, model input and processing settings
Display follows modulated Model — makes the display show the model the MODEL input has selected rather than the one the knob picked. It is on the Options submenu
Display channel — picks which polyphonic channel the model display reports. It is on the Options submenu
C0 model modulation (monophonic) — reads the MODEL input as note pitches from C0 to B1, picking the model outright rather than offsetting the knob. It is on the Options submenu
Low CPU (disable resampling) — runs the models at the engine sample rate instead of resampling, which costs less processing and adds aliasing. It is on the Options submenu
Custom data — the submenu for the data the six-operator FM, wave terrain and wavetable models read
Load... — reads a custom data file into the model in use; it appears only while one of the five models that take custom data is selected. It is on the Custom data submenu
Reset to factory default — puts the built-in data back into the model in use. It is on the Custom data submenu
Open editors in web browser... — opens the maker's web page for building custom data files. It is on the Custom data submenu
